facts.statement: The genus Alectrosaurus was formally described by Charles Gilmore in 1933.
facts.quote: authority: Gilmore, 1933

facts.statement: Alectrosaurus lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 96 million years ago, in the Iren Dabasu Formation.
facts.quote: Alectrosaurus (; meaning "alone lizard") is a genus of tyrannosauroid theropod dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous period, about some 96 million years ago in what is now the Iren Dabasu Formation.

facts.statement: Alectrosaurus was a medium-sized, bipedal carnivore estimated to be 5 to 6 meters long with a body shape similar to Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: It was a medium-sized, moderately-built, ground-dwelling, bipedal carnivore, estimated at 5 to 6 m with a body shape similar to its much larger advanced relative, Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: Alectrosaurus was likely a fast-running pursuit predator, a trait indicated by its elongated hindlimbs that was lost in later, more robust tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: Alectrosaurus was a very fast running tyrannosauroid as indicated by the elongated hindlimbs that likely filled the niche of a pursuit predator, a trait that seems to be lost by the advanced and robust tyrannosaurids, in adulthood.

facts.statement: A second specimen, catalogued as AMNH 6368, was discovered by George Olsen approximately 30 meters away from the holotype on May 4.
facts.quote: On May 4, Olsen discovered another specimen approximately 30 m away from his first find, catalogued as AMNH 6368.

facts.statement: The fossils were found in the Iren Dabasu Formation, located in what is now the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region of China.
facts.quote: These discoveries were made at the Iren Dabasu Formation in what is now the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region (Nei Mongol Zizhiqu) of China.

facts.statement: The name Alectrosaurus translates to "alone lizard" or "mateless lizard", derived from Greek words meaning alone and lizard.
facts.quote: The generic name, Alectrosaurus, can be translated as "alone lizard" or "mateless lizard", derived from the Greek words ἄλεκτρος (meaning alone or unmarried) and σαῦρος (meaning lizard).

facts.statement: The species name olseni honors George Olsen, the discoverer of the first specimens.
facts.quote: The specific name, olseni, is in honor of George Olsen, who discovered the first specimens.

facts.statement: Alectrosaurus reached a length of 5 to 6 meters and a weight between 454 and 907 kilograms.
facts.quote: It was a medium-sized tyrannosauroid, reaching a length between 5 and 6 m, and a weight ranging from 454 to 907 kg.

facts.statement: Alectrosaurus had a femur and tibia of nearly equal length, contrasting with most other tyrannosauroids where the tibia is longer.
facts.quote: The length of its tibia (shinbone) and femur (thighbone) are very close, in contrast to the majority of other tyrannosauroids, where the tibia is longer.

facts.statement: The femur of Alectrosaurus measures 72.7 cm and the tibia measures 73 cm.
facts.quote: The femur measures 72.7 cm and the tibia 73 cm.

facts.statement: Alectrosaurus is distinguished by long slender limbs, a long and slender humerus, a robust and curved first digit, and a femur and tibia of subequal length.
facts.quote: Following the original description of Alectrosaurus, it can be distinguished by the following traits: long slender-limbed type of tyrannosauroid; humerus long and slender; ungual and phalanx of digit I robust, laterally compressed and strongly curved; femur and tibia subequal in length; length of astragalus onefourth the combined length of astragalus and tibia.

facts.statement: Gilmore classified Alectrosaurus as a "Deinodont," a term now considered equivalent to tyrannosaurid, based on similarities in manual unguals and hindlimbs.
facts.quote: He based this on his observation that the manual unguals from both specimens were morphologically similar. Observing similarities with the hindlimbs of specimen AMNH 5664 Gorgosaurus sternbergi, he classified this new genus as a "Deinodont", a term that is now considered equivalent to tyrannosaurid.

facts.statement: Due to its fragmentary nature, there is little confidence in Alectrosaurus's relationships with other tyrannosauroids, and many recent analyses have omitted it.
facts.quote: Due to its fragmentary nature, there is presently very little confidence in restoring its relationships with other tyrannosauroids and many recent cladistic analyses have omitted it altogether.

facts.statement: Some paleontologists have considered Alectrosaurus olseni to be a species of Albertosaurus.
facts.quote: Some paleontologists have equivocally considered Alectrosaurus olseni to be a species of Albertosaurus.

facts.statement: In 2022, Thomas Carr suggested that certain Mongolian specimens previously linked to Alectrosaurus may not belong to the genus due to unique tyrannosaurid traits.
facts.quote: In 2022, Thomas Carr noted that these specimens may not be referable to Alectrosaurus, because of some tyrannosaurid traits found in the Mongolian specimens which the holotype does not possess.

facts.statement: The elongated digits and metatarsals of Alectrosaurus suggest it was a fast-running pursuit predator, similar to terrestrial runner birds.
facts.quote: The hindlimb of the specimen AMNH 6554 is notable for the particular elongated digits and metatarsals, differing from other tyrannosauroids. These traits are found in terrestrial runner birds, suggesting that Alectrosaurus was suited as a fast-running tyrannosauroid dinosaur with well developed hindlimbs; probably a pursuit predator.

facts.statement: Alectrosaurus has a high cursorial-limb-proportion score of 16.5, which is higher than most carnosaurs.
facts.quote: Alectrosaurus was recovered with a relatively high CLP (Cursorial-limb-proportion) score at 16.5, higher than most carnosaurs.

facts.statement: A 2001 study found no signs of stress fractures in 23 foot bones examined from Alectrosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2001, a study conducted by Bruce Rothschild and colleagues, examined 23 foot bones referred to Alectrosaurus for signs of stress fractures, but none were found.

facts.statement: The genus name Alectrosaurus means 'bachelor lizard' because no two skeletons were ever found together.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se debe a que nunca se hallaron dos esqueletos juntos de este dinosaurio.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Alectrosaurus was a hind limb discovered in the Iren Dabasu Formation in Inner Mongolia, China.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo (AMNH 6554) de Alectrosaurus era un miembro posterior descubierto en Formación Iren Dabasu de la región autónoma de Mongolia Interior en China.

facts.statement: The genus and species were named by American paleontologist Charles W. Gilmore in 1933.
facts.quote: El género y las especies fueron nombrados por el paleontólogo estadounidense Charles W. Gilmore en 1933.

facts.statement: Alectrosaurus and Gigantoraptor were the top predators of their paleoenvironment and preyed on ornithischians like Bactrosaurus and Gilmoreosaurus.
facts.quote: Alectrosaurus y Gigantoraptor eran los depredadores superiores de su paleoambiente y se aprovecharon de los ornitisquios como Bactrosaurus y Gilmoreosaurus.

facts.statement: Alectrosaurus was a bipedal carnivore with a body shape similar to its much larger relative, Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: Era un carnívoro bípedo con una forma del cuerpo similar a su pariente mucho más grande, Tyrannosaurus rex.

facts.statement: Alectrosaurus was much smaller than T. rex, likely around 5 meters long, 2 meters high, and weighing an estimated 600 kg.
facts.quote: Alectrosaurus era sin embargo mucho más pequeño, muy probablemente de alrededor de 5 metros de largo y 2 de alto, exhibiendo un peso estimado de 600 kg.

facts.statement: The length of Alectrosaurus's tibia and femur were very similar, contrasting with most other tyrannosauroids where the tibia is longer.
facts.quote: La longitud de su tibia y el fémur están muy cerca, en contraste con la mayoría de los otros tiranosáuridos, donde la tibia es más larga.

facts.statement: In a 2001 study, 23 foot bones from Alectrosaurus were examined for stress fractures, but none were found.
facts.quote: En un estudio de 2001 realizado por Bruce Rothschild y otros paleontólogos, 23 huesos del pie se refiere Alectrosaurus se examinaron en busca de signos de fractura por estrés, pero no se encontraron ninguno.

facts.statement: Although Alectrosaurus is undoubtedly included in Tyrannosauroidea, its exact position within the family is debated due to fragmentary nature, and many recent cladistic analyses have omitted it.
facts.quote: Aunque indudablemente está incluido en Tyrannosauroidea, se duda debido a su naturaleza fragmentaria de su posición exacta con respecto a los otros de su familia y muchos análisis cladísticos recientes la han omitido en conjunto.

facts.statement: Some paleontologists consider Alectrosaurus olseni to be a species of Albertosaurus.
facts.quote: Algunos paleontólogos consideran a Alectrosaurus olseni como una especie de Albertosaurus.

facts.statement: Alectrosaurus was originally characterized as a theropod with long arms, but this was due to a mistaken association with forelimb elements from a Therizinosauroidea.
facts.quote: Alectrosaurus fue caracterizado originalmente como terópodo de largos brazos, pero esto era debido a la asociación equivocada con elementos del miembro anterior de un Therizinosauroidea.

facts.statement: The age of the Iren Dabasu Formation is unclear, but it is commonly cited as Campanian, Late Cretaceous, approximately 83 to 74 million years ago.
facts.quote: La edad de esta formación geológica no está clara, pero comúnmente se cita como perteneciente al Campaniense durante el Cretácico superior hace aproximadamente 83 a 74 millones de años atrás.

facts.statement: Additional fossils, including hind limb material, a skull, and shoulder elements, referred to Alectrosaurus were found in the Bayan Shireh Formation of Mongolia, which also has an uncertain age.
facts.quote: Más fósiles, incluyendo material comparable del miembro posterior así como un cráneo y elementos del hombro, han sido referidos a Alectrosaurus. Estos fósiles fueron encontrados en Formación Bayan Shireh de Mongolia, una formación que también es de edad incierta.

facts.statement: The time range for Alectrosaurus is estimated from the Cenomanian to Campanian stages, between 100.5 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Campanian (100.5 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: A cladistic analysis showed that collections of specimens relate more to each other than to any other taxon, suggesting they are at least closely linked, if not the same species.
facts.quote: Un análisis cladístico demostró que las colecciones de especímenes se relacionan más entre sí que con cualquier otro taxón, así que están probablemente por lo menos estrechamente vinculados, si no son la misma especie.

rejected.quote: On April 25 in the gobi desert, assistant paleontologist George Olsen excavated and recovered the holotype AMNH FARB 6554, a nearly complete right hindlimb.
